paragraphs.title: Request of the chiefs of Gilead

easy.question: Who came to Moses at the beginning of the chapter?
answers: The chief fathers of the families of the sons of Gilead
All the people of Israel
Only the tribe of Levi
easy.explanation: Verse 1 explicitly says the chief fathers of the families of the sons of Gilead came near to Moses.

easy.question: How is it said the land should be given according to verse 2?
answers: By the decision of each family
By lot (by drawing lots)
Only according to the will of the Lord
easy.explanation: Verse 2 says the land is to be given 'by lot' — the distribution is by lot, not by private decision.

easy.question: According to what is said in verse 2 — to whom was Zelophehad's inheritance given?
answers: To his sons only
To another tribe
To his daughters
easy.explanation: Verse 2 states the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother was given to his daughters.

medium.question: What did the chiefs fear about the marriages of Zelophehad's daughters?
answers: That it would cause their tribe's inheritance to be reduced if a portion passed into another tribe
That it would cancel the commandments
That it would enlarge the inheritance of their tribes
medium.explanation: In verse 3 they express concern that their portion would be 'taken from the lot of our inheritance' if the daughters married into another tribe — i.e., the inheritance could pass to another tribe through marriage.

medium.question: In the phrase 'be taken from the lot of our inheritance', what does 'be taken from' mean in context?
answers: Be added to the inheritance
Be diminished/removed from the inheritance
Remain unchanged
medium.explanation: The context shows the fear that the inheritance would be removed or diminished from their lot if it passed to another tribe.

medium.question: Who are the 'families of the sons of Joseph' mentioned in verse 5?
answers: The tribes of Simeon and Levi
The tribes of Judah and Simeon
The tribes of the sons of Joseph (Ephraim and Manasseh)
medium.explanation: The traditional reading identifies the families of Joseph as the two tribes descended from Joseph: Ephraim and Manasseh.

challenge.question: According to the leaders' logic in the chapter — what happens if the daughters marry within their father's tribe?
answers: The inheritance remains within the tribe and is not diminished
The inheritance passes to another tribe
The inheritance becomes the property of the whole people
challenge.explanation: The leaders were only worried about marriages into other tribes; if the daughters married within their father's tribe the inheritance would stay in the tribe.

challenge.question: In verse 4 the phrase reads 'and when the jubilee of the children of Israel shall be'. What does 'the jubilee' refer to here?
answers: A new festival observed by Israel
The year of Jubilee when property is to return to original owners
The name of a new leader
challenge.explanation: The term 'jubilee' refers to the Jubilee year in which inheritances could revert to original owners — a legal concept affecting land distribution.

challenge.question: Why did the leaders address 'before Moses and before the princes, the chief fathers' instead of only Moses?
answers: So Moses wouldn't hear and their words would be forgotten
Because it was a private matter only about the daughters
So the ruling would be public and agreed on by the princes and all Israel
challenge.explanation: They brought the matter before the princes and chief fathers so the decision would be public and binding for the tribes, not a private ruling by one person.

questions.question: According to the leaders' logic in the chapter — what happens if the daughters marry within their father's tribe?
answers: The inheritance remains within the tribe and is not diminished
The inheritance passes to another tribe
The inheritance becomes the property of the whole people
questions.explanation: The leaders were only worried about marriages into other tribes; if the daughters married within their father's tribe the inheritance would stay in the tribe.

answers: A new festival observed by Israel
The year of Jubilee when property is to return to original owners
The name of a new leader
questions.explanation: The term 'jubilee' refers to the Jubilee year in which inheritances could revert to original owners — a legal concept affecting land distribution.

questions.question: Why did the leaders address 'before Moses and before the princes, the chief fathers' instead of only Moses?
answers: So Moses wouldn't hear and their words would be forgotten
Because it was a private matter only about the daughters
So the ruling would be public and agreed on by the princes and all Israel
questions.explanation: They brought the matter before the princes and chief fathers so the decision would be public and binding for the tribes, not a private ruling by one person.

paragraphs.title: The LORD's ruling concerning the daughters

easy.question: Who issued the law described in these verses?
answers: Moses
The LORD
Aaron
easy.explanation: The passage begins 'This is the thing which the LORD commanded...' — the command comes from the LORD.

easy.question: What is said in verse 6 about the marriages of Zelophehad's daughters?
answers: They may marry whoever they like
They must remain unmarried within the family
They shall marry and be part of the family of their father's tribe
easy.explanation: The verse allows them to marry but stipulates they 'shall be to the family of the tribe of their father' — meaning marriages within their father's tribe.

easy.question: What is the repeated prohibition in verses 7 and 9?
answers: That an inheritance be transferred from tribe to tribe
That one can inherit from grandchildren
That land be sold to a foreigner
easy.explanation: Both verses explicitly state the prohibition that an inheritance shall not be transferred from one tribe to another.

medium.question: Why does the law prohibit transferring an inheritance from one tribe to another as stated in the verses?
answers: So the tribes of Israel will inherit the land of their fathers
Because daughters are not allowed to inherit at all
To allow exchange of inheritance between tribes
medium.explanation: The text states the aim is 'that each of the children of Israel may keep himself to the inheritance of his fathers' — preserving tribal inheritances.

medium.question: In the phrase 'shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers', what does 'keep himself to the inheritance' mean?
answers: To stick physically
To be stuck at a job
To remain belonging and loyal to their inheritance/tribe
medium.explanation: Here it means to remain attached to one’s tribal inheritance — to belong to and stay with the inheritance of one’s fathers.

medium.question: According to verse 8, why must a daughter who inherits 'be wife to one of the family of the tribe of her father'?
answers: So that the children of Israel may each inherit the possession of their fathers
To make the inheritance common to the whole people
To deprive daughters of inheritance rights
medium.explanation: The verse states the purpose: so that each man among Israel may retain the inheritance of his fathers.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of the phrase 'neither shall the inheritance remove' in verses 7 and 9 emphasize?
answers: A strong warning meant to prevent inheritance moving between tribes
That the law applies only to Zelophehad's family
That the intent is to broaden the distribution to more descendants
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording functions as legal emphasis: the prohibition on moving inheritance between tribes is strong and binding.

challenge.question: What does the wording 'they shall be to the families of the tribe of their father' imply about the daughters' status?
answers: Daughters receive independent inheritance outside the tribe
Daughters lose all inheritance rights
Daughters remain, for inheritance purposes, members of their father's tribe
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates they marry within their father's tribal family, so regarding inheritance they remain part of their father's tribe.

challenge.question: How was this law expected to affect tribal land distribution over generations?
answers: Prevent transfer of land between tribes and preserve tribal boundaries
Encourage sale of land to neighboring tribes
Lead to merging of tribes and wide transfers of land
challenge.explanation: By forbidding inheritance to pass from tribe to tribe, the law maintains stability of tribal land holdings across generations.

questions.question: What does the repetition of the phrase 'neither shall the inheritance remove' in verses 7 and 9 emphasize?
answers: A strong warning meant to prevent inheritance moving between tribes
That the law applies only to Zelophehad's family
That the intent is to broaden the distribution to more descendants
questions.explanation: The repeated wording functions as legal emphasis: the prohibition on moving inheritance between tribes is strong and binding.

questions.question: What does the wording 'they shall be to the families of the tribe of their father' imply about the daughters' status?
answers: Daughters receive independent inheritance outside the tribe

questions.explanation: The phrase indicates they marry within their father's tribal family, so regarding inheritance they remain part of their father's tribe.

answers: Prevent transfer of land between tribes and preserve tribal boundaries

questions.explanation: By forbidding inheritance to pass from tribe to tribe, the law maintains stability of tribal land holdings across generations.

paragraphs.title: Implementation of the ruling — marriages and inheritance

easy.question: Who did as the LORD commanded Moses in verse 10?
answers: The daughters of Zelophehad
The men of Manasseh
The tribe of Levi
easy.explanation: Verse 10 explicitly says the daughters of Zelophehad did as the LORD commanded Moses.

easy.question: How many names of Zelophehad's daughters are listed in verse 11?
answers: Four
Five
Six
easy.explanation: Five names are listed: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah.

easy.question: Whose son is Manasseh according to verse 12?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Joseph
easy.explanation: Verse 12 calls them 'the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph' — Manasseh is Joseph's son.

medium.question: In 'their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father', what does 'their inheritance' refer to?
answers: Their parcel of land / hereditary rights
Their wages for work
A family name
medium.explanation: In context 'their inheritance' denotes the land or hereditary rights the daughters received; the verse states these stayed in their father's tribal family.

medium.question: Why is it specified that they married 'into the families of the sons of Manasseh'?
answers: To move their inheritance to a different tribe
To ensure their inheritance remained in their father's tribe
To show that they left the land
medium.explanation: They married within families of Manasseh so that their inheritance would remain with their father's tribe, as required.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'as the LORD commanded Moses' in verse 10 express?
answers: That this was only Moses' opinion
That they disobeyed the command
That they acted according to a divine command
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates they acted in accordance with a command given by the LORD to Moses.

challenge.question: How can the phrase 'to their fathers' brothers' sons' be understood?
answers: They married their paternal cousins (their fathers' brothers' sons)
They married men from a completely different tribe
They took their father's family name
challenge.explanation: 'Their fathers' brothers' sons' refers to paternal relatives — i.e., cousins — so they married within their extended paternal family.

challenge.question: The fact the verse uses the plural 'families' regarding the sons of Manasseh suggests that:
answers: They married all the families of Israel
They married into different families within the tribe of Manasseh
They married outside the tribe of Manasseh
challenge.explanation: The plural indicates marriages into more than one family or clan within the tribe of Manasseh, not a single family.

challenge.question: What cultural/legal conclusion follows from verse 12: 'and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father'?
answers: Women lost inheritance rights when they married
Their inheritance passed to their husbands at marriage
The law allowed women to retain inheritance within their father's tribe
challenge.explanation: The verse states their inheritance stayed in their father's tribe, indicating the law permitted women to keep their inheritance within their paternal tribe rather than transferring it to their husband's tribe.

questions.question: How can the phrase 'to their fathers' brothers' sons' be understood?
answers: They married their paternal cousins (their fathers' brothers' sons)
They married men from a completely different tribe
They took their father's family name
questions.explanation: 'Their fathers' brothers' sons' refers to paternal relatives — i.e., cousins — so they married within their extended paternal family.

questions.question: The fact the verse uses the plural 'families' regarding the sons of Manasseh suggests that:
answers: They married all the families of Israel
They married into different families within the tribe of Manasseh
They married outside the tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: The plural indicates marriages into more than one family or clan within the tribe of Manasseh, not a single family.

questions.question: What cultural/legal conclusion follows from verse 12: 'and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father'?
answers: Women lost inheritance rights when they married
Their inheritance passed to their husbands at marriage
The law allowed women to retain inheritance within their father's tribe
questions.explanation: The verse states their inheritance stayed in their father's tribe, indicating the law permitted women to keep their inheritance within their paternal tribe rather than transferring it to their husband's tribe.

paragraphs.title: Place and giving of the commandments

easy.question: What does the phrase 'These are the commandments and the judgments' in the verse indicate?
answers: A list of instructions and laws
A list of people
A description of the landscape
easy.explanation: The verse introduces 'commandments and judgments' — that is, instructions and laws given to the people.

easy.question: According to the verse, through whom were these commandments and judgments given?
answers: The people
Moses
The LORD
easy.explanation: The verse says these were commanded by the LORD 'by the hand of Moses' — Moses is the mediator through whom the commandments were given.

easy.question: To which people were these commandments given according to the verse?
answers: The children of Moab
Only the priests
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse states these commandments were given by Moses to the children of Israel.

medium.question: Where were the commandments and judgments given, as stated in the verse?
answers: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
At Sinai
In the land of Canaan after entry
medium.explanation: The verse specifies the location: 'in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho.'

medium.question: What does the word 'judgments' mean in the phrase 'the commandments and the judgments'?
answers: Names of people
Laws and rulings; legal and social directives
Geographical places
medium.explanation: 'Judgments' here refers to legal rulings or regulations; together with 'commandments' it denotes a body of law.

medium.question: What does the verse imply about how the commandments were delivered?
answers: They were given directly to each person without a mediator
They were given through Moses as mediator between the LORD and Israel
They were invented by the leaders of Moab
medium.explanation: It states the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses — indicating Moses served as the mediator who communicated the divine commandments to Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the choice of the place 'in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho' about the timing of these commandments?
answers: They were given just before entering the Promised Land, near the border
They refer to the much later period of the Judges
They relate to the Exodus from Egypt
challenge.explanation: The geographic reference near the Jordan and Jericho places the event just before the people entered Canaan, i.e., on the edge of the Promised Land.

challenge.question: What historical-geographic information can be learned from mentioning 'Moab' and 'Jericho' in the verse?
answers: That Moab is the name of a central priest
That the location is specific, marking a border area by the Jordan and toward Jericho
That it refers to an area not identifiable in translation
challenge.explanation: Mentioning Moab and Jericho identifies a specific area east of the Jordan near the border of the Promised Land.

challenge.question: What is the linguistic and legal significance of the pairing 'the commandments and the judgments' in the context of the Torah?
answers: It refers only to ritual commandments without social aspects
It indicates a full legal system that includes civil and social laws as well as religious commands
It refers to mere statements without binding force
challenge.explanation: The phrase denotes a comprehensive set of rules: 'commandments' (often ritual duties) and 'judgments' (legal/social ordinances), implying binding legislation for the community.
